 with Si Shailendra.

Ms. Akshara Santhosh, Advocate fo
 R-2 with R-2 in person.
CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJNISH BHATNAGAR  ORDER % 22.03.2023 CRL.M.A. 7538/2023 (Exemption) Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
The application stand disposed of.

1. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.84/2021, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Bharat Nagar, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 19.06.2020 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as husband and wife with each other.
Thereafter, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since 13.09.2020.
On 19.02.2021, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have Aman Aggarwal & Ors vs State Through Sho Ps Bharat Nagar & Anr on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53412922/
1 settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement dated 07.07.2022 arrived at before the Mediation Centre, Rohini Courts, Delhi.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13-B(2) of the HMA was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree dated 12.01.2023 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Courts, Rohini, Delhi.

entities.text: Principal Judge, Family Courts, Rohini, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The copy of the decree is already on record.
5. Petitioners and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and they have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs. 2,00,000/- (bearing no. 003070 dated 02.03.2023 drawn on Bandhan Bank) has been handed over to respondent no.2.
Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
6. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.84/2021, under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Bharat Nagar, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
8.

The present petition stands disposed of accordingly RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J MARCH 22,
